title: Saul's conversion on the Damascus road + Peter heals Aeneas and raises Tabitha

paragraphs.text: But Saul, yet breathing threatening and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went unto the high priest,
paragraphs.original: Ὁ δὲ Σαῦλος ἔτι ἐμπνέων ἀπειλῆς καὶ φόνου εἰς τοὺς μαθητὰς τοῦ κυρίου, προσελθὼν τῷ ἀρχιερεῖ
paragraphs.translit: Ho de Saulos eti empneōn apeilēs kai phonou eis tous mathētas tou kyriou, proselthōn tō archierei

paragraphs.text: and asked of him letters to Damascus unto the synagogues, that if he found any that were of the Way, whether men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.
paragraphs.original: ᾐτήσατο παρʼ αὐτοῦ ἐπιστολὰς εἰς Δαμασκὸν πρὸς τὰς συναγωγάς, ὅπως ἐάν τινας εὕρῃ τῆς ὁδοῦ ὄντας, ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας, δεδεμένους ἀγάγῃ εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ.
paragraphs.translit: ētēsato parʼ autou epistolas eis Damaskon pros tas synagōgas, hopōs ean tinas heurē tēs hodou ontas, andras te kai gynaikas, dedemenous agagē eis Ierousalēm.

paragraphs.text: And as he journeyed, it came to pass that he drew nigh unto Damascus: and suddenly there shone round about him a light out of heaven:
paragraphs.original: ἐν δὲ τῷ πορεύεσθαι ἐγένετο αὐτὸν ἐγγίζειν τῇ Δαμασκῷ, ἐξαίφνης τε αὐτὸν περιήστραψεν φῶς ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: en de tō poreuesthai egeneto auton engizein tē Damaskō, exaiphnēs te auton periēstrapsen phōs ek tou ouranou,

paragraphs.text: and he fell upon the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
paragraphs.original: καὶ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἤκουσεν φωνὴν λέγουσαν αὐτῷ Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;
paragraphs.translit: kai pesōn epi tēn gēn ēkousen phōnēn legousan autō Saoul Saoul, ti me diōkeis;

paragraphs.text: And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And he [said], I am Jesus whom thou persecutest:
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δέ· Τίς εἶ, κύριε; ὁ δέ· Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὃν σὺ διώκεις·
paragraphs.translit: eipen de· Tis ei, kyrie; ho de· Egō eimi Iēsous hon sy diōkeis·

paragraphs.text: but rise, and enter into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ ἀνάστηθι καὶ εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν πόλιν, καὶ λαληθήσεταί σοι ὅ τί σε δεῖ ποιεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: alla anastēthi kai eiselthe eis tēn polin, kai lalēthēsetai soi ho ti se dei poiein.

paragraphs.text: And the men that journeyed with him stood speechless, hearing the voice, but beholding no man.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἄνδρες οἱ συνοδεύοντες αὐτῷ εἱστήκεισαν ἐνεοί, ἀκούοντες μὲν τῆς φωνῆς μηδένα δὲ θεωροῦντες.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de andres hoi synodeuontes autō heistēkeisan eneoi, akouontes men tēs phōnēs mēdena de theōrountes.

paragraphs.text: And Saul arose from the earth; and when his eyes were opened, he saw nothing; and they led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus.
paragraphs.original: ἠγέρθη δὲ Σαῦλος ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς, ἀνεῳγμένων δὲ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτοῦ οὐδὲν ἔβλεπεν· χειραγωγοῦντες δὲ αὐτὸν εἰσήγαγον εἰς Δαμασκόν.
paragraphs.translit: ēgerthē de Saulos apo tēs gēs, aneōgmenōn de tōn ophthalmōn autou ouden eblepen· cheiragōgountes de auton eisēgagon eis Damaskon.

paragraphs.text: And he was three days without sight, and did neither eat nor drink.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἦν ἡμέρας τρεῖς μὴ βλέπων, καὶ οὐκ ἔφαγεν οὐδὲ ἔπιεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēn hēmeras treis mē blepōn, kai ouk ephagen oude epien.

paragraphs.text: Now there was a certain disciple at Damascus, named Ananias; and the Lord said unto him in a vision, Ananias. And he said, Behold, I [am here], Lord.
paragraphs.original: Ἦν δέ τις μαθητὴς ἐν Δαμασκῷ ὀνόματι Ἁνανίας, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐν ὁράματι ὁ κύριος· Ἁνανία. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἰδοὺ ἐγώ, κύριε.
paragraphs.translit: Ēn de tis mathētēs en Damaskō onomati Hananias, kai eipen pros auton en horamati ho kyrios· Hanania. ho de eipen· Idou egō, kyrie.

paragraphs.text: And the Lord [said] unto him, Arise, and go to the street which is called Straight, and inquire in the house of Judas for one named Saul, a man of Tarsus: for behold, he prayeth;
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἀναστὰς πορεύθητι ἐπὶ τὴν ῥύμην τὴν καλουμένην Εὐθεῖαν καὶ ζήτησον ἐν οἰκίᾳ Ἰούδα Σαῦλον ὀνόματι Ταρσέα, ἰδοὺ γὰρ προσεύχεται,
paragraphs.translit: ho de kyrios pros auton· Anastas poreuthēti epi tēn rhymēn tēn kaloumenēn Eutheian kai zētēson en oikia Iouda Saulon onomati Tarsea, idou gar proseuchetai,

paragraphs.text: and he hath seen a man named Ananias coming in, and laying his hands on him, that he might receive his sight.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶδεν ἄνδρα ἐν ὁράματι Ἁνανίαν ὀνόματι εἰσελθόντα καὶ ἐπιθέντα αὐτῷ χεῖρας ὅπως ἀναβλέψῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eiden andra en horamati Hananian onomati eiselthonta kai epithenta autō cheiras hopōs anablepsē.

paragraphs.text: But Ananias answered, Lord, I have heard from many of this man, how much evil he did to thy saints at Jerusalem:
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ Ἁνανίας· Κύριε, ἤκουσα ἀπὸ πολλῶν περὶ τοῦ ἀνδρὸς τούτου, ὅσα κακὰ τοῖς ἁγίοις σου ἐποίησεν ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ·
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē de Hananias· Kyrie, ēkousa apo pollōn peri tou andros toutou, hosa kaka tois hagiois sou epoiēsen en Ierousalēm·

paragraphs.text: and here he hath authority from the chief priests to bind all that call upon thy name.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὧδε ἔχει ἐξουσίαν παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων δῆσαι πάντας τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους τὸ ὄνομά σου.
paragraphs.translit: kai hōde echei exousian para tōn archiereōn dēsai pantas tous epikaloumenous to onoma sou.

paragraphs.text: But the Lord said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles and kings, and the children of Israel:
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος· Πορεύου, ὅτι σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς ἐστίν μοι οὗτος τοῦ βαστάσαι τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐνώπιον ἐθνῶν τε καὶ βασιλέων υἱῶν τε Ἰσραήλ,
paragraphs.translit: eipen de pros auton ho kyrios· Poreuou, hoti skeuos eklogēs estin moi houtos tou bastasai to onoma mou enōpion ethnōn te kai basileōn hyiōn te Israēl,

paragraphs.text: for I will show him how many things he must suffer for my name`s sake.
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ γὰρ ὑποδείξω αὐτῷ ὅσα δεῖ αὐτὸν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματός μου παθεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: egō gar hypodeixō autō hosa dei auton hyper tou onomatos mou pathein.

paragraphs.text: And Ananias departed, and entered into the house; and laying his hands on him said, Brother Saul, the Lord, [even] Jesus, who appeared unto thee in the way which thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mayest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Spirit.
paragraphs.original: ἀπῆλθεν δὲ Ἁνανίας καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν, καὶ ἐπιθεὶς ἐπʼ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας εἶπεν· Σαοὺλ ἀδελφέ, ὁ κύριος ἀπέσταλκέν με, Ἰησοῦς ὁ ὀφθείς σοι ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ᾗ ἤρχου, ὅπως ἀναβλέψῃς καὶ πλησθῇς πνεύματος ἁγίου.
paragraphs.translit: apēlthen de Hananias kai eisēlthen eis tēn oikian, kai epitheis epʼ auton tas cheiras eipen· Saoul adelphe, ho kyrios apestalken me, Iēsous ho ophtheis soi en tē hodō hē ērchou, hopōs anablepsēs kai plēsthēs pneumatos hagiou.

paragraphs.text: And straightway there fell from his eyes as it were scales, and he received his sight; and he arose and was baptized;
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὐθέως ἀπέπεσαν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν ὡς λεπίδες, ἀνέβλεψέν τε καὶ ἀναστὰς ἐβαπτίσθη,
paragraphs.translit: kai eutheōs apepesan autou apo tōn ophthalmōn hōs lepides, aneblepsen te kai anastas ebaptisthē,

paragraphs.text: and he took food and was strengthened. And he was certain days with the disciples that were at Damascus.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λαβὼν τροφὴν ἐνίσχυσεν. Ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ τῶν ἐν Δαμασκῷ μαθητῶν ἡμέρας τινὰς,
paragraphs.translit: kai labōn trophēn enischysen. Egeneto de meta tōn en Damaskō mathētōn hēmeras tinas,

paragraphs.text: And straightway in the synagogues he proclaimed Jesus, that he is the Son of God.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὐθέως ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ἐκήρυσσεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eutheōs en tais synagōgais ekēryssen ton Iēsoun hoti houtos estin ho hyios tou theou.

paragraphs.text: And all that heard him were amazed, and said, Is not this he that in Jerusalem made havoc of them that called on this name? and he had come hither for this intent, that he might bring them bound before the chief priests.
paragraphs.original: ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες οἱ ἀκούοντες καὶ ἔλεγον· Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ πορθήσας ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους τὸ ὄνομα τοῦτο, καὶ ὧδε εἰς τοῦτο ἐληλύθει ἵνα δεδεμένους αὐτοὺς ἀγάγῃ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς;
paragraphs.translit: existanto de pantes hoi akouontes kai elegon· Ouch houtos estin ho porthēsas en Ierousalēm tous epikaloumenous to onoma touto, kai hōde eis touto elēlythei hina dedemenous autous agagē epi tous archiereis;

paragraphs.text: But Saul increased the more in strength, and confounded the Jews that dwelt at Damascus, proving that this is the Christ.
paragraphs.original: Σαῦλος δὲ μᾶλλον ἐνεδυναμοῦτο καὶ συνέχυννεν τοὺς Ἰουδαίους τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐν Δαμασκῷ, συμβιβάζων ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστός.
paragraphs.translit: Saulos de mallon enedynamouto kai synechynnen tous Ioudaious tous katoikountas en Damaskō, symbibazōn hoti houtos estin ho christos.

paragraphs.text: And when many days were fulfilled, the Jews took counsel together to kill him:
paragraphs.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληροῦντο ἡμέραι ἱκαναί, συνεβουλεύσαντο οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀνελεῖν αὐτόν·
paragraphs.translit: Hōs de eplērounto hēmerai hikanai, synebouleusanto hoi Ioudaioi anelein auton·

paragraphs.text: but their plot became known to Saul. And they watched the gates also day and night that they might kill him:
paragraphs.original: ἐγνώσθη δὲ τῷ Σαύλῳ ἡ ἐπιβουλὴ αὐτῶν. παρετηροῦντο δὲ καὶ τὰς πύλας ἡμέρας τε καὶ νυκτὸς ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀνέλωσιν·
paragraphs.translit: egnōsthē de tō Saulō hē epiboulē autōn. paretērounto de kai tas pylas hēmeras te kai nyktos hopōs auton anelōsin·

paragraphs.text: but his disciples took him by night, and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.
paragraphs.original: λαβόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ νυκτὸς διὰ τοῦ τείχους καθῆκαν αὐτὸν χαλάσαντες ἐν σπυρίδι.
paragraphs.translit: labontes de hoi mathētai autou nyktos dia tou teichous kathēkan auton chalasantes en spyridi.

paragraphs.text: And when he was come to Jerusalem, he assayed to join himself to the disciples: and they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.
paragraphs.original: Παραγενόμενος δὲ εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἐπείραζεν κολλᾶσθαι τοῖς μαθηταῖς· καὶ πάντες ἐφοβοῦντο αὐτόν, μὴ πιστεύοντες ὅτι ἐστὶν μαθητής.
paragraphs.translit: Paragenomenos de eis Ierousalēm epeirazen kollasthai tois mathētais· kai pantes ephobounto auton, mē pisteuontes hoti estin mathētēs.

paragraphs.text: But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles, and declared unto them how he had seen the Lord in the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how at Damascus he had preached boldly in the name of Jesus.
paragraphs.original: Βαρναβᾶς δὲ ἐπιλαβόμενος αὐτὸν ἤγαγεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους, καὶ διηγήσατο αὐτοῖς πῶς ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶδεν τὸν κύριον καὶ ὅτι ἐλάλησεν αὐτῷ καὶ πῶς ἐν Δαμασκῷ ἐπαρρησιάσατο ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Barnabas de epilabomenos auton ēgagen pros tous apostolous, kai diēgēsato autois pōs en tē hodō eiden ton kyrion kai hoti elalēsen autō kai pōs en Damaskō eparrēsiasato en tō onomati tou Iēsou.

paragraphs.text: And he was with them going in and going out at Jerusalem,
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἦν μετʼ αὐτῶν εἰσπορευόμενος καὶ ἐκπορευόμενος εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, παρρησιαζόμενος ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ κυρίου,
paragraphs.translit: kai ēn metʼ autōn eisporeuomenos kai ekporeuomenos eis Ierousalēm, parrēsiazomenos en tō onomati tou kyriou,

paragraphs.text: preaching boldly in the name of the Lord: and he spake and disputed against the Grecian Jews; but they were seeking to kill him.
paragraphs.original: ἐλάλει τε καὶ συνεζήτει πρὸς τοὺς Ἑλληνιστάς· οἱ δὲ ἐπεχείρουν ἀνελεῖν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: elalei te kai synezētei pros tous Hellēnistas· hoi de epecheiroun anelein auton.

paragraphs.text: And when the brethren knew it, they brought him down to Caesarea, and sent him forth to Tarsus.
paragraphs.original: ἐπιγνόντες δὲ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ κατήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς Καισάρειαν καὶ ἐξαπέστειλαν αὐτὸν εἰς Ταρσόν.
paragraphs.translit: epignontes de hoi adelphoi katēgagon auton eis Kaisareian kai exapesteilan auton eis Tarson.

paragraphs.text: So the church throughout all Judaea and Galilee and Samaria had peace, being edified; and, walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, was multiplied.
paragraphs.original: Ἡ μὲν οὖν ἐκκλησία καθʼ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Γαλιλαίας καὶ Σαμαρείας εἶχεν εἰρήνην οἰκοδομουμένη, καὶ πορευομένη τῷ φόβῳ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ τῇ παρακλήσει τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐπληθύνετο.
paragraphs.translit: Hē men oun ekklēsia kathʼ holēs tēs Ioudaias kai Galilaias kai Samareias eichen eirēnēn oikodomoumenē, kai poreuomenē tō phobō tou kyriou kai tē paraklēsei tou hagiou pneumatos eplēthyneto.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, as Peter went throughout all parts, he came down also to the saints that dwelt at Lydda.
paragraphs.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ Πέτρον διερχόμενον διὰ πάντων κατελθεῖν καὶ πρὸς τοὺς ἁγίους τοὺς κατοικοῦντας Λύδδα.
paragraphs.translit: Egeneto de Petron dierchomenon dia pantōn katelthein kai pros tous hagious tous katoikountas Lydda.

paragraphs.text: And there he found a certain man named Aeneas, who had kept his bed eight years; for he was palsied.
paragraphs.original: εὗρεν δὲ ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπόν τινα ὀνόματι Αἰνέαν ἐξ ἐτῶν ὀκτὼ κατακείμενον ἐπὶ κραβάττου, ὃς ἦν παραλελυμένος.
paragraphs.translit: heuren de ekei anthrōpon tina onomati Ainean ex etōn oktō katakeimenon epi krabattou, hos ēn paralelymenos.

paragraphs.text: And Peter said unto him, Aeneas, Jesus Christ healeth thee: arise and make thy bed. And straightway he arose.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος· Αἰνέα, ἰᾶταί σε Ἰησοῦς Χριστός· ἀνάστηθι καὶ στρῶσον σεαυτῷ· καὶ εὐθέως ἀνέστη.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autō ho Petros· Ainea, iatai se Iēsous Christos· anastēthi kai strōson seautō· kai eutheōs anestē.

paragraphs.text: And all that dwelt at Lydda and in Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶδαν αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ κατοικοῦντες Λύδδα καὶ τὸν Σαρῶνα, οἵτινες ἐπέστρεψαν ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον.
paragraphs.translit: kai eidan auton pantes hoi katoikountes Lydda kai ton Sarōna, hoitines epestrepsan epi ton kyrion.

paragraphs.text: Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did.
paragraphs.original: Ἐν Ἰόππῃ δέ τις ἦν μαθήτρια ὀνόματι Ταβιθά, ἣ διερμηνευομένη λέγεται Δορκάς· αὕτη ἦν πλήρης ἔργων ἀγαθῶν καὶ ἐλεημοσυνῶν ὧν ἐποίει.
paragraphs.translit: En Ioppē de tis ēn mathētria onomati Tabitha, hē diermēneuomenē legetai Dorkas· hautē ēn plērēs ergōn agathōn kai eleēmosynōn hōn epoiei.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass in those days, that she fell sick, and died: and when they had washed her, they laid her in an upper chamber.
paragraphs.original: ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ἀσθενήσασαν αὐτὴν ἀποθανεῖν· λούσαντες δὲ ἔθηκαν αὐτὴν ἐν ὑπερῴῳ.
paragraphs.translit: egeneto de en tais hēmerais ekeinais asthenēsasan autēn apothanein· lousantes de ethēkan autēn en hyperōō.

paragraphs.text: And as Lydda was nigh unto Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men unto him, entreating him, Delay not to come on unto us.
paragraphs.original: ἐγγὺς δὲ οὔσης Λύδδας τῇ Ἰόππῃ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Πέτρος ἐστὶν ἐν αὐτῇ ἀπέστειλαν δύο ἄνδρας πρὸς αὐτὸν παρακαλοῦντες· Μὴ ὀκνήσῃς διελθεῖν ἕως ἡμῶν·
paragraphs.translit: engys de ousēs Lyddas tē Ioppē hoi mathētai akousantes hoti Petros estin en autē apesteilan dyo andras pros auton parakalountes· Mē oknēsēs dielthein heōs hēmōn·

paragraphs.text: And Peter arose and went with them. And when he was come, they brought him into the upper chamber: and all the widows stood by him weeping, and showing the coats and garments which Dorcas made, while she was with them.
paragraphs.original: ἀναστὰς δὲ Πέτρος συνῆλθεν αὐτοῖς· ὃν παραγενόμενον ἀνήγαγον εἰς τὸ ὑπερῷον, καὶ παρέστησαν αὐτῷ πᾶσαι αἱ χῆραι κλαίουσαι καὶ ἐπιδεικνύμεναι χιτῶνας καὶ ἱμάτια ὅσα ἐποίει μετʼ αὐτῶν οὖσα ἡ Δορκάς.
paragraphs.translit: anastas de Petros synēlthen autois· hon paragenomenon anēgagon eis to hyperōon, kai parestēsan autō pasai hai chērai klaiousai kai epideiknymenai chitōnas kai himatia hosa epoiei metʼ autōn ousa hē Dorkas.

paragraphs.text: But Peter put them all forth, and kneeled down and prayed; and turning to the body, he said, Tabitha, arise. And she opened her eyes; and when she saw Peter, she sat up.
paragraphs.original: ἐκβαλὼν δὲ ἔξω πάντας ὁ Πέτρος καὶ θεὶς τὰ γόνατα προσηύξατο, καὶ ἐπιστρέψας πρὸς τὸ σῶμα εἶπεν· Ταβιθά, ἀνάστηθι. ἡ δὲ ἤνοιξεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῆς, καὶ ἰδοῦσα τὸν Πέτρον ἀνεκάθισεν.
paragraphs.translit: ekbalōn de exō pantas ho Petros kai theis ta gonata prosēuxato, kai epistrepsas pros to sōma eipen· Tabitha, anastēthi. hē de ēnoixen tous ophthalmous autēs, kai idousa ton Petron anekathisen.

paragraphs.text: And he gave her his hand, and raised her up; and calling the saints and widows, he presented her alive.
paragraphs.original: δοὺς δὲ αὐτῇ χεῖρα ἀνέστησεν αὐτήν, φωνήσας δὲ τοὺς ἁγίους καὶ τὰς χήρας παρέστησεν αὐτὴν ζῶσαν.
paragraphs.translit: dous de autē cheira anestēsen autēn, phōnēsas de tous hagious kai tas chēras parestēsen autēn zōsan.

paragraphs.text: And it became known throughout all Joppa: and many believed on the Lord.
paragraphs.original: γνωστὸν δὲ ἐγένετο καθʼ ὅλης τῆς Ἰόππης, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν πολλοὶ ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον.
paragraphs.translit: gnōston de egeneto kathʼ holēs tēs Ioppēs, kai episteusan polloi epi ton kyrion.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, that he abode many days in Joppa with one Simon a tanner.
paragraphs.original: ἐγένετο δὲ ἡμέρας ἱκανὰς μεῖναι ἐν Ἰόππῃ παρά τινι Σίμωνι βυρσεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: egeneto de hēmeras hikanas meinai en Ioppē para tini Simōni byrsei.
